mainTopic: רקב of a מת: which corpse dust carries טומאה, and what counts as a mixture (גלגלין)
overview: The משנה listed a ladle-full of רקב (decayed corpse dust) as a טומאה that makes a נזיר shave, and this amud asks which dust counts. A ברייתא teaches that the dust must come only from the body, not mixed with cloth, wood, or brick. עולא adds that it must come from flesh, גידים, and bones together, and he defends this against רבא's challenges. רבי יוחנן rules that two bodies buried together become a mixture (גלגלין). רבא explains that the teaching calling dust from two bodies טמא is about bodies that rotted separately. רבי יוחנן also rules that cut hair buried with the body makes a mixture, which leads to חזקיה's question about hair that is ready to be cut but still attached. רבי ירמיה then asks about dust that comes by way of the heel, and that question ends in תיקו. Finally, he asks whether a dead עובר inside its mother forms a mixture with her, and the follow-up question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Which corpse has dust that carries impurity
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that only a body buried with nothing that can rot along with it (naked, in marble or on stone) has רקב. If it was buried in clothes, in wood, or on bricks, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Which dead body has the law of רקב? A body that was buried naked in a marble coffin or on a stone floor. That one has רקב. But if it was buried in its clothes, in a wooden coffin, or on a brick floor, it does not have רקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains which buried body produces dust that counts as טמא רקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marble and stone do not crumble into dust, so any dust found there must be from the body itself. Clothes, wood, and bricks do crumble, so the dust is mixed with other material. The ברייתא shows that רקב must be pure body dust, not a mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: Decayed dust of a dead body

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for the whole section: רקב must come only from the body. Everything that follows asks what exactly counts as coming from the body.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ מֵת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רָקָב?
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Which dead body has the law of dust?
phrases.notes: "The law of dust" means its rotted dust carries the special טומאה of רקב.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת שֶׁנִּקְבַּר עָרוֹם בְּאָרוֹן שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ
phrases.english: A body that was buried naked in a marble coffin

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי רִצְפָּה שֶׁל אֲבָנִים —
phrases.english: or on top of a stone floor —
this is a body that has the law of dust.
If it was buried in its cloak, in a wooden coffin,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי רִצְפָּה שֶׁל לְבֵנִים —
phrases.english: or on top of a brick floor —
this is a body that does not have the law of dust.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ מֵת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רָקָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the משנה's term רקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a body buried with nothing that can decay alongside it produces טמא רקב.

steps.title: עולא: dust must come from flesh, sinews, and bones together
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that רקב counts only if it comes from all three parts of the body: flesh, גידים, and bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Dust only counts as רקב if it comes from the flesh, the sinews, and the bones.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא adds a new requirement: the dust must come from all three parts of the body together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the dust must come only from the body. עולא goes further and says it must come from the whole body, meaning flesh, גידים, and bones. Dust from just one part does not count.

phrases.english: Ulla said: It is not dust,
unless it comes from the flesh
and from the sinews and from the bones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: אֵין רָקָב, אֶלָּא הַבָּא מִן הַבָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further requirement to the ברייתא's rule about pure body dust.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רקב is only dust that comes from flesh, sinews, and bones together.

steps.title: רבא: a teaching implies bone dust alone is impure
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a teaching that dust from flesh is טהור, and infers that dust from bone is טמא even without flesh. That goes against עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged עולא: It was taught that dust that comes from the flesh is pure. That implies that dust from the bone is impure, even though there is no flesh in it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks עולא's rule with a teaching that seems to show bone dust alone is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching only says flesh dust is pure. רבא reads it as a contrast: bone dust must be impure. If bone dust alone is impure, then עולא is wrong that all three parts are needed.

phrases.english: Rava challenged Ulla:
Dust that comes from the flesh is pure.
This implies that from the bone it is impure,
even though there is no flesh!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רָבָא לְעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's rule from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that רקב must come from flesh, sinews, and bones together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching implies that bone dust without flesh is טמא, so not all three parts are needed.

steps.title: עולא rereads the teaching: flesh is pure unless bone is mixed in
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the teaching should be read differently: flesh dust is pure unless there is bone with it. Then the teaching supports needing flesh and bone together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it like this: Dust that comes from the flesh is pure, unless there is bone in the flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא defends himself by changing how we read the teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא read the teaching as "flesh is pure, but bone is impure." עולא reads it as "flesh alone is pure, but flesh with bone is impure." Now the teaching does not show that bone alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Say it like this (read it this way)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the teaching shows that bone dust alone is טמא. With עולא's reading, the opposite case to plain flesh dust is flesh dust with bone in it, not bone dust by itself.

phrases.english: Say it like this:
Dust that comes from the flesh is pure,
unless there is bone in the flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the inference of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching implies that bone dust alone is טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching implies that only flesh combined with bone is טמא.

steps.title: But the teaching never mentions sinews
steps.stepSummary: Even with עולא's reading, the teaching mentions only flesh and bone, not גידים. So it still does not match עולא's rule that sinews are needed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are no sinews mentioned!
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge continues: עולא's new reading still leaves out the sinews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said all three parts are needed. His reading of the teaching covers flesh and bone, but says nothing about גידים. So the teaching still seems to argue with him.

phrases.english: But there are no sinews!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לֵיכָּא גִּידִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to attack עולא's answer from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rereading of the teaching in step 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reread teaching requires flesh and bone only, but עולא requires sinews too.

steps.title: Flesh and bones always come with sinews
steps.stepSummary: Answer: there cannot be flesh and bones without sinews, so sinews are automatically included.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is impossible to have flesh and bones without sinews.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that sinews do not need to be mentioned, because they are always there with flesh and bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a real body, flesh and bone are always joined by גידים. So dust that comes from flesh and bone must also include sinew. The teaching fits עולא after all.
steps.whatToRemember: עולא's rule stands: רקב must come from flesh, sinews, and bones. A teaching that mentions only flesh and bone still fits, because sinews always come along with them.

phrases.english: It is impossible for flesh and bones
to be without sinews.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבָשָׂר וְלַעֲצָמוֹת בְּלֹא גִּידִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual reality: one element necessarily includes another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching leaves out sinews, so it argues with עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sinews are always present with flesh and bones, so they are included without being mentioned.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: two bodies buried together become a mixture
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that two bodies buried together count as a mixture, so their dust is not the רקב of one body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Two bodies that were buried together become a mixture with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling: dust from two bodies buried together is treated as a mixture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned that רקב must be pure dust of the body, with nothing else mixed in. רבי יוחנן says another body also counts as "something else." So two bodies buried together ruin each other's רקב status.

keyTerms.meaning: A mixture; something that spoils the other's purity of source

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי מֵתִים שֶׁקְּבָרָן זֶה עִם זֶה —
phrases.english: Two bodies that were buried with one another —
become a mixture for one another.
phrases.notes: "גלגלין" means each body is like an outside ingredient for the other, like the clothes or wood in the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about רקב: mixing dust of two bodies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two bodies buried together become a mixture, so their dust is not the רקב of a single body.

steps.title: רב נתן: a teaching says dust from two bodies is impure
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן challenges רבי יוחנן from a teaching that dust from two bodies is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן challenged: But it was taught that dust that comes from two bodies is impure!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נתן attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling with a teaching that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said two bodies spoil each other's רקב. But a teaching says dust from two bodies is טמא. That seems to directly argue with him.

phrases.english: Rav Natan raises a challenge:
Dust that comes from two bodies is impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that two bodies buried together become a mixture.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching says dust from two bodies is טמא, so two bodies do not spoil each other's רקב.

steps.title: רבא explains the case of dust from two bodies
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the teaching about two bodies is talking about two bodies buried separately, each turning to dust on its own. Together they made one full ladle of dust.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The teaching is talking about a case where they buried this body by itself and that body by itself. Each one rotted, and together they added up to a full ladle of dust.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רבי יוחנן against רב נתן's challenge. He shows that the teaching is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said two bodies buried together form a mixture, so their dust is not רקב. רבא says the teaching that calls the dust טמא is talking about bodies buried separately. Each rotted as its own body, and only the amount was combined to reach a full ladle.

keyTerms.meaning: A ladle. 'מְלֹא תַּרְווֹד' (a full ladle) is the amount of corpse dust that makes things טמא
The rotted dust of a dead body

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Buried TOGETHER means a mixture, so the dust is not רקב. Buried SEPARATELY means each pile is real רקב, and the two piles can add up to a full ladle.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: שֶׁקָּבְרוּ זֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: Rava said: Where they buried this one by itself
and that one by itself, and they rotted,
and they came to a full ladle of dust.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שֶׁקָּבְרוּ זֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נתן's challenge to רבי יוחנן from step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the teaching to a specific case (bodies buried separately)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching seemed to say that dust from two bodies buried together is טמא, which goes against רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching is about two bodies that rotted separately and only add up to the amount together, so רבי יוחנן's rule about bodies buried together still stands

steps.title: Cut hair buried with the body makes a mixture
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: if a dead person's hair was cut and buried with him, the hair becomes a mixture (גלגלין) with his dust.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone cut a dead person's hair and buried it with him, it becomes a mixture for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another rule about corpse dust. Cut hair buried with the body mixes in with the dust.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the two bodies buried together, cut hair is something extra mixed in with the body. So the dust is no longer pure רקב of one body, and it does not get the special טומאה of a full ladle of רקב.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'mixture': extra material mixed into the dust, so it no longer counts as pure רקב

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If one cut his hair and buried it with him —
phrases.notes: 'His hair' means the dead person's hair.

phrases.english: it becomes a mixture for him.
phrases.notes: Because it is mixed in, his dust no longer counts as the רקב of one body.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another 'mixture' rule for רקב, similar in idea to רבי יוחנן's ruling about two bodies
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cut hair buried with a body makes a mixture, so the dust is not counted as רקב

steps.title: משנה: teeth, hair and nails are not טמא unless attached
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: everything in a dead body is טמא except teeth, hair and nails. But while they are still attached, they are all טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: Everything in a dead body is טמא, except the teeth, the hair and the nails. But while they are attached, they are all טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a background source from another משנה. This sets up חזקיה's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teeth, hair and nails do not carry טומאה when they are on their own. They are treated as part of the body only while they are attached to it. This attached-or-not rule is exactly what חזקיה will ask about.

phrases.english: We learned there: Everything in a corpse is impure,
phrases.notes: 'There' is a משנה in מסכת אהלות.

phrases.english: except for the teeth, the hair, and the nails.
But while they are attached — they are all impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related משנה about hair to set up the next question
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teeth, hair and nails of a corpse are not טמא when separate, but they are טמא while attached

steps.title: חזקיה asks about hair and nails ready to be cut
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה asks: what about hair or nails that are ready to be cut? Are they treated as already cut, or as still attached?
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה asked: Hair that is ready to be shaved, or a nail that is ready to be cut, what is the law? Do we say anything ready to be cut is treated as cut? Or maybe, right now at least, they are still attached?
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה asks a question about the משנה from step 11. He gives two possible ways to think about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: something about to be cut is treated as already cut, so it is not טמא. Side two: we only look at how things are right now, and right now it is attached, so it is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a question he was unsure about)
Anything ready to be cut is treated as if already cut

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya asked: His hair that is ready to be shaved,
a nail that is ready to be cut, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן: כׇּל הָעוֹמֵד לִיגָּזֵז כְּגָזוּז דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: Do we say: anything ready to be cut is like it is cut,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא הַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא הָא מְחוּבָּרִין?
phrases.english: or perhaps, now at least, they are attached?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי חִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a question on the משנה about attached hair and nails
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is hair or a nail that is ready to be cut treated as already cut (not טמא) or as still attached (טמא)?

steps.title: Try to answer חזקיה from רבה בר בר חנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests answering חזקיה from רבה בר בר חנה: he said cut hair is a mixture, which hints that uncut hair is not, even if it is ready to be cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us answer the question from רבה בר בר חנה. The reason it is a mixture is because he cut the hair. That means if he did not cut it, it is not a mixture.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer חזקיה's question using רבה בר בר חנה's ruling from step 10. Step 14 will push this proof away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה said 'if one cut' the hair. The exact wording suggests that only cut hair makes a mixture. So hair that is ready to be cut but still attached counts as attached, which would answer חזקיה.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us answer (solve) the question
But then (meaning: in the opposite case)

phrases.aramaic: וְנִיפְשׁוֹט לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: And let him answer it from Rabba bar bar Ḥana:
The reason is because he cut it,
but if he did not cut it — not!
phrases.notes: Meaning: uncut hair would not be a mixture, even if it was ready to be cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִיפְשׁוֹט לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer חזקיה's question from רבה בר בר חנה's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading רבה בר בר חנה's words exactly: only cut hair makes a mixture, so uncut hair, even if ready to be cut, counts as attached
steps.raayaObject: That hair which is ready to be cut but still attached counts as attached (not as cut).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן: hair that was cut (גזז) and buried with the body is a mixture, which implies that uncut hair is not.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה was unsure about uncut hair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the proof. רבה בר בר חנה only meant that cut hair is surely a mixture. About uncut hair, he himself had the same question.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: If he cut it, it is a mixture. If he did not cut it, he is unsure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 13. So חזקיה's question stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'if he cut it' does not mean uncut hair is surely different. רבה בר בר חנה only ruled on the clear case of cut hair. The uncut case was a question for him too.

keyTerms.meaning: He is unsure about it; it is a question for him

steps.whatToRemember: Cut hair buried with a body is surely a mixture. Hair that is ready to be cut but still attached is an open question.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי קָאָמַר: גָּזַז — הֲרֵי זֶה גַּלְגַּלִּים.
phrases.english: This is what he is saying: If he cut it — it is a mixture.
If he did not cut it — it is a question for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the attempt to answer חזקיה from רבה בר בר חנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference from 'if he cut' is wrong. רבה בר בר חנה only ruled on cut hair and was himself unsure about uncut hair.

steps.title: Does dust that comes from the heel count?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether רקב that comes from the heel has the same law as רקב that comes from the whole body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: what is the law of dust that comes from the heel? Maybe the law we learned only covers dust that comes from the whole dead body, and not dust that comes from the heel. Or maybe there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a new question about רקב. Does dust that comes from the heel get the same law as dust that comes from the whole body?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law of רקב was learned as a tradition, and it may only cover dust from the entire body. Dust from the heel might fall outside it. Or the heel might be no different from the rest of the body.

keyTerms.meaning: The dust left after a dead body rots

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
Dust that comes from the heel, what is its law?
When we learned the law of dust,
it was dust that comes from the whole dead body,
but dust that comes from the heel, no,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question about the dust of a dead body. It continues the general topic of what counts as רקב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רקב that comes from the heel counts as real corpse dust, just like dust from the whole body.

steps.title: Trying to prove it from dust of two bodies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי נתן ברבי אושעיא: dust from two dead bodies is טמא. If heel dust did not count, each body's dust would be in doubt, so heel dust must count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי נתן ברבי אושעיא taught that dust coming from two dead bodies is טמא. If you thought dust from the heel does not count, then for this body maybe the dust came from the heel, and for that body maybe it also came from the heel. Yet he calls it טמא for sure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבי ירמיה's question from a teaching of רבי נתן ברבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן rules that dust from two bodies is definitely טמא. If heel dust did not count, then for each body we could worry that its dust came from the heel, and there would be a doubt. Since he rules it is definitely טמא, heel dust must count too.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rabbi Natan son of Rabbi Oshaya taught:
Dust that comes from two dead bodies is impure.
And if you would think
that dust coming from the heel does not count,
go to this body:
perhaps its dust came by way of the heel,
and this body too: perhaps its dust came by way of the heel?
phrases.notes: Since רבי נתן calls it definitely טמא, the proof argues that the heel worry doesn't matter. The next step pushes this proof away.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבִּי נָתָן בְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That רקב coming from the heel counts as corpse dust.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נתן ברבי אושעיא: dust from two dead bodies is טמא, with no worry that it came from the heel.

steps.title: The proof only covers a whole rotted body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that when the whole body rotted, dust coming by way of the heel surely counts. The real question is when only one limb rotted and the dust came by way of the heel.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the whole body rotted and the dust came out by way of the heel, then yes, it surely counts. But the question here is when only one limb rotted and the dust came out by way of the heel. What is the law then?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. רבי נתן's case does not touch the real question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן is talking about whole bodies that rotted. Dust from a whole rotted body counts even if it comes out by way of the heel. רבי ירמיה is really asking about a case where only one limb rotted, and the proof says nothing about that.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying heel dust never counts. It agrees that heel dust from a whole rotted body counts. It only leaves open the case where just one limb rotted.

phrases.english: If the whole dead body rotted
and the dust came by way of the heel, so too, it counts.
Rather, here it is talking about a case
where one limb rotted,
and the dust came by way of the heel. What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּאִירְקִיב כּוּלֵּיהּ מֵת וְקָאָתֵי דֶּרֶךְ עָקֵב הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 16 by narrowing the question of step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the proof, but only by narrowing the case. The גמרא agrees that heel dust from a whole rotted body counts.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי נתן's case is about whole rotted bodies, while the open question is about dust from one rotted limb that comes by way of the heel.

steps.title: The heel question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question about one rotted limb is left open: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the question stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the proof pushed away, nothing else settles the narrowed case. So the question about dust from one rotted limb that comes by way of the heel stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand (the question stays unanswered)

steps.whatToRemember: Dust from a whole rotted body counts even if it comes by way of the heel. Dust from one rotted limb that comes by way of the heel is a question left open (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the branch opened in step 15 after the proof was rejected in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The case of one rotted limb whose dust comes by way of the heel stays unresolved.

steps.title: Is an unborn baby part of its mother or separate?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether a dead עובר inside its dead mother is a mixture (גלגלין) with her. Is it part of her body, or a separate thing because it was going to come out?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: a fetus inside a woman, is it a mixture or not? Since מר said a fetus is like its mother's thigh, it is part of her body and not a mixture. Or perhaps, since it will end up coming out, it is already separate from her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a new question. Does a dead עובר inside its dead mother count as something separate mixed in with her, like the cut hair in step 10?
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says an עובר is like a limb of its mother ("עובר ירך אמו"), so it is simply her body and not a mixture. The other side says that because it is meant to be born, it is already treated as separate from her.

keyTerms.meaning: A mixture (something separate mixed into the dust)
A fetus is like its mother's thigh (part of her body)
It will end up coming out

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
A fetus in a woman's womb,
is it a mixture, or not?
Since the Master said
a fetus is like its mother's thigh,
therefore it is her body,
and it is not a mixture,
or perhaps, since it will end up coming out,
it is considered separated from her.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: עוּבָּר בִּמְעֵי אִשָּׁה, הָוֵי גַּלְגַּלִּים, אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question that uses the idea of גלגלין from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a dead עובר inside its dead mother is part of her body, or a separate body that forms a mixture with her.

steps.title: Setting up a follow-up question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a follow-up: even if we say the עובר is separate from its mother, a further question remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that a fetus, which will end up coming out, is considered separated from her,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It says, "Even if you decide the עובר is separate," and is about to ask a further question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "ואם תמצי לומר" picks one side of the last question and builds on it. It takes the side that the עובר is separate from its mother, and a new question will follow.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (even if we decide this way)

phrases.english: And if you will say
that a fetus, which will end up coming out,
is considered separated from her,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the second side of step 19, that the עובר is separate, as the basis for a further question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A further question that comes up even if the עובר is separate from its mother. It is asked in the text that follows.
